one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes the first half of a WWIII-hotspots pair -- concluded the following Sunday in B14. WWIII can erupt in three hot spots: (1) the South China Sea (also called West Philippine Sea) and East China Sea, (2) Ukraine, and (3) the Middle East -- in all of which two or more of the seven nuclear powers (US, Russia, China, UK, France, Israel, Iran) are major players. SOUTH AND EAST CHINA SEAS: China is building civilian and military facilities with 'defense and offense capabilities' in the Spratlys and other SCS islets -- also claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, and Taiwan -- and is reclaiming huge tracts in eight islets, including an airstrip in an 800-hectare reclamation. In the adjacent East China Sea, China has a bitter confrontation with Japan: it claims 'undisputed sovereignty' and denies Unclos applicability in the Spratlys yet asserts Unclos-recognized EEZ in the East China Sea. It also asserts sovereignty over the Senkaku Islands (Diaoyu in Chinese) -- under Japan's control with oil/gas reserves below -- and on November 23, 2013 declared an Air Defense Identification Zone (Adiz) requiring all aircraft (including over Senkaku) to file flight plans and submit radio/transponder information; Japan said it would not comply. Lately the US has joined the fray, diverting 60 percent (up from 40 percent) of its powerful navy to the SCS/East China Seas; a few days ago it heralded the deployment to Japan of the USS Ronald Reagan, the largest nuclear-powered aircraft carrier in the world, with battleships, cruisers, and destroyers. The Chinese have not yet placed offensive military installations (like missile silos) on reclaimed islets -- but if -- repeat, if -- they send missile-carrying warships, the US may declare a blockade the way Kennedy did in October 1962 when Khrushchev sent missile-carrying vessels to Cuba. Fortunately Khrushchev backed off; will China back off similarly? If not, WWIII could erupt in our backyard. RUSSIA AND UKRAINE: upon the 1991 Soviet collapse, Russia and Ukraine became independent states with uneasy relations as Ukraine veered West, repulsing Russian overtures. About 20% of Ukrainians have Russian roots. Last year, after a controversial referendum, Russia annexed Crimea; separatist forces armed with Russian-made heavy weapons fought the Ukrainian military and occupied Donbass, Donetsk, and Lugansk. President Poroshenko avows the separatists are disguised Russian regulars; Putin denies. Russia stationed about 40,000 troops on the border conducting war games. WWIII risk arises if Russian troops openly cross the border to aid separatists, or if an important military/political leader is slain -- recalling that WWII began with Hitler's blitz of Poland and WWI was ignited after Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie were killed by Serb militants. THE MIDDLE EAST is complicated: in Yemen, Saudi Arabia supports the government while Iran arms rebel Houthis; the US backs the Saudis with logistics and intelligence -- but not much else. Yet the US and Iran are together in assisting the ragtag Iraqi army against the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS). To the chagrin of Saudi Arabia and Israel (America's staunchest ME ally), the US is spearheading a 10-year move to lift trade sanctions against Iran in exchange for Iran's dubious vow to moderate its nuclear ambitions. Hawkish Israeli PM Netanyahu is so enraged that he threatens to unleash a preemptive nuclear strike on Iran -- if he does, the world will be plunged into a holocaust because Iran can retaliate in kind. The Saudis are also inconsolable at US reconciliation overtures and demonstrate their disaffection through the sudden decline of crude-oil prices to discourage US shale extraction and to undercut it at viable commercial prices.
